request: a simple block-building sandbox game with a 32x32 block world
thesis: A tiny world you can reshape: every click changes a cell, and the 32x32 grid is small enough to read at a glance and finish a build in minutes.
job: open the file and see a 32x32 world
pick a block type from a palette
place blocks by click or drag
see what is selected and where the cursor is
save the world and have it back after reload
switch layer or view to judge the build

tricks: hover ghost shows where block lands
tests: can a stranger build a house in 60s
does every click visibly change state

tricks: prevent context menu so right-click erases
pointer events cover mouse and touch

principles: blocks read as material not flat colour
tricks: lighten top edge, darken bottom edge for bevel
noise speckle per cell for texture
tests: palette swatches distinguishable at small size

principles: state in a 2D array, render from state

kinds.name: top-down grid painter
kinds.what: flat 2D map where each cell is a block type

kinds.name: isometric stack builder
kinds.what: cells hold height columns shown in iso view

descriptions: each block type has base colour plus top-light bevel and noise speckle
start with a little pre-made terrain so the world isn't a blank void
behaviors: clear empties to sky; reset restores starter terrain

descriptions: status line shows x,y and block under cursor

anti_keywords.not: 3D engine, physics, crafting, inventory, mobs, multiplayer
anti_keywords.instead: simple means place and remove blocks, nothing else
canvas scales to width, pointer coordinates mapped by bounding rect
one array is the truth, render from it

checks: click a cell: its block changes and count updates
